summary: Technical sync to align on Redwood marketplace adapter, packaging (Helm + operator), telemetry hooks and canary/autoscale policies for Venari's hybrid edge deployment. Focus on quantization tradeoffs, KMS compatibility, and minimal footprint for cold-start sensitive flows.
questions: Can Redwood's adapter run as sidecar or does it require dedicated GPU pool?
What is the smallest supported instance for 1k TPS burst?
How are audit logs exported to customer's SIEM?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-22 08:00 PT | Duration: ~54 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luca (Redwood SE), Maya (Venari Platform Lead), Arjun (Venari Edge Architect), Hannah (Venari Security), Dave (Venari DevOps)

Auto-summary: quick alignment on packaging and telemetry. Agree to run perf lab and share Helm chart stub.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 55 minutes, um we wanted to focus on the adapter lifecycle and how we'll surface telemetry into your ops stack. quick intros?
00:10 Maya (Venari): thanks Jordan, i'm Maya, lead for platform at Venari, Arjun and Hannah are on too, and Dave who runs our k8s infra.
00:18 Arjun (Venari): hey all, want to make sure the adapter can operate in our air-gapped edge clusters and talk about quantization/latency tradeoffs, that's the big one.
00:26 Priya (Redwood SE): great, that's exactly why we asked for this sync. i'll walk through the packaging options, then Luca will show telemetry hooks, then we can go into quant and evict caching and autoscale.

02:05 Priya (Redwood SE): packaging first — there are two patterns we've seen: 1) Helm + operator that manages model artifacts and node selectors for dedicated GPU pools, 2) lightweight sidecar mode that proxies requests to a regional Redwood Dedicated endpoint for tiny edge nodes. both have pros/cons.
02:30 Dave (Venari): sidecar sounds simpler for us, less ops, but i'm worried about latency if traffic goes out to region. we need p95 under 250ms for the inference path.
02:38 Priya: agreed, sidecar usually adds network roundtrip. the trade is you can offload heavy models to hosted/dedicated and keep tiny nodes cheap. we can also configure prefix caching and local kv-cache to reduce p95.
03:05 Arjun: can we pin certain routes to local runtime? we want deterministic latency for safety-critical flows.
03:14 Luca (Redwood): yes, with our routing policy you can pin model variants to local pools; for deterministic low-latency we recommend dedicated inference on a local rack or small edge GPU with a quantized model. that's where quantization matrix Priya mentioned comes in.

05:00 Priya: quick note on packaging — our Helm chart includes optional sidecar values and operator CRD samples. It supports pulling OCI model bundles and can be configured to use private registry credentials and a customer KMS for keys.
05:18 Maya: OCI model bundles — is there size limit we should know about? we have models that are 6-8GB after q4_8 quant.
05:25 Priya: existing threshold is fine up to 10–12GB per artifact. operator handles streaming pulls and delta patches. for air-gapped we provide signed artifacts you can mirror.

07:40 Hannah (Venari): security — audit logs and KMS: our security team requires HSM-backed keys and that we retain audit logs 2 years. can Redwood integrate with our HashiCorp Vault/HSM?
07:54 Jordan: yes, we support KMS integrations and can work with Vault; for HSM there is an on-prem variant. we'll share the KMS compatibility matrix. audit logs can be forwarded via OpenTelemetry to your SIEM or S3/GCS with lifecycle rules.
08:15 Hannah: who owns log encryption at rest?
08:20 Priya: the adapter can encrypt logs at rest using customer-managed keys. there are a couple of modes: logs encrypted by Redwood KMS in hosted mode, or by your KMS in private mode. we'll put details in the refarch doc.

10:02 Luca (Redwood): telemetry hooks — we ship an OpenTelemetry collector sidecar that emits traces, spans and metrics with a standard schema: latency per route, model version, token count, cache hit ratio, evicted kv cache. you can plug it into your OTEL pipeline or use our telemetry endpoint.
10:28 Dave: can we map trace IDs back to request IDs in our ingested logs? our tracing pipeline expects a certain header.
10:34 Luca: yes we propagate x-request-id and traceparent. small mismatch sometimes if sidecar rewrites headers, but we preserve them by default.

12:00 Maya: okay quantization — Arjun you'll kick this off, but we need to understand perf impact vs quality. can Redwood provide examples?
12:10 Priya: we prepared a quant/latency tradeoff matrix. for your candidate models, q4_0 yields ~1.8x speedup with slight drop in logits for long-range context, while q8_0 yields better quality but higher memory. i'll attach the spreadsheet.
12:28 Arjun: can we get a quick A/B test plan? we'd like to keep canary at 5% traffic for 48 hours before ramp.
12:35 Priya: yes our rollout supports canary policies and automatic fallback if generation quality drops below a threshold. we'll export metrics for your eval set.

15:00 Jordan: on marketplace listing specifics — Venari wants a private listing for enterprise customers and a public listing for the community. there are different packaging requirements for each.
15:18 Maya: right, we need the private listing to support tenant isolation and billing through our marketplace. can Redwood marketplace handle private offers?
15:25 Jordan: yes, our marketplace supports private offers with private endpoints plus entitlement checks. Billing integration depends on partner marketplace — we'll share the partner playbook for integration.

18:20 Dave: deployment question — what is the recommended autoscale policy for bursty inference? our traffic shows long tails with sudden spikes.
18:30 Priya: we suggest a hybrid policy: keep a small warm pool (min replicas) and autoscale on in-flight tokens + queue depth. also configure prefix/KV cache so repeated prefixes don't spin up new instances. we can share sample HPA/CA configs.
18:50 Arjun: do you support GPU pooling across nodes for better utilization?
18:56 Luca: yes, Dedicated mode supports multi-tenant GPU pools with scheduling and soft-affinity. operator will ensure cold-starts are minimized via prefetch and lazy KV prewarm.

22:40 Hannah: compliance — can Redwood provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and do you support tenant-level audit logs?
22:47 Jordan: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestations; for private deployments we can surface tenant-scoped audit logs. we'll share the security pack and an NDA if needed.

25:00 Priya: perf lab plan — propose a 2-hour lab where we run your real traffic replay against quantized variants and sidecar vs dedicated. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost. propose week of 10/27.
25:20 Maya: that works for us, we'll prepare the traffic profile and SLOs.

28:10 Dave: connectivity — in air-gapped sites, how do you handle model updates?
28:18 Luca: operator supports signed delta patches; we ship an artifact bundle that your ops team can mirror via a secure USB or internal registry sync. the install script validates signatures and uses your KMS to unwrap secrets.

31:45 Arjun: telemetry retention — we store metrics short-term locally then forward to central cluster. is there an option to sample events to reduce bandwidth?
31:55 Luca: yes you can sample traces and metrics at the collector. for traces we do head-based or probabilistic sampling. for critical flows you can force full sampling.

34:00 Priya: another point — fallback policies. if a local edge node becomes overloaded we can route to regional Dedicated or Redwood Hosted variant. the routing policy is pluggable so you can set cost vs latency preferences.
34:25 Maya: we want deterministic fail-open behavior for critical safety endpoints; can that be guaranteed?
34:32 Jordan: we'd model that as highest-priority route pinned to local; fallback requires explicit approval. we can implement a hard fail policy for certain tags.

38:10 Hannah: audit trail for rollouts — we need immutable records of who changed model versions and when. does the operator capture that?
38:18 Luca: yes the operator logs changes, records GitOps diffs if you use a GitOps flow, and signs rollout events. we can forward to your SIEM.

41:00 Priya: open question from our side — do you have internal latency budgets per tenant that we should encode into the canary policy?
41:08 Maya: yes, our platform SLOs are p95 <250ms, p99 <450ms for edge-critical customers. non-critical can be softer. we'll send a list of customers who need strict SLAs.

44:10 Jordan: quick competitor note — you mentioned earlier GoliathAI; how much of this is motivated by their pricing/latency story?
44:17 Maya: they undercut cost but we saw quality issues. we're trying to balance cost and deterministic latency for our customers.

46:30 Dave: operational playbook — can Redwood attach runbooks for incident scenarios? e.g. model regression detected, fallback engaged.
46:40 Luca: absolutely, we'll include incident runbooks, playbook examples and script snippets in the repo.

49:00 Priya: wrap-up: agreed next steps — we'll run the perf lab, share Helm chart stub, you provide traffic profile and KMS constraints. also send security pack.
49:12 Maya: perfect. one more thing — can we get a quick estimate for reserved Dedicated pricing for a 3-node edge cluster? we need ballpark to prep budget.
49:22 Jordan: we'll send an initial pricing ballpark in the follow-up email, subject to capacity and region.

52:00 Jordan: ok thanks everyone, i'll recap in email and attach action items. meeting adjourned.

End transcript.
